title: What If a Town Had a Population of One? She Pays Taxes to Herself

scenes.text: What if a whole town had one resident? She is the mayor, and she taxes herself.
Monowi, Nebraska. In the 1930s, 150 people lived here, with shops, restaurants, even a jail. Then the farms failed.
In 2004 the last resident's husband died. The 2010 census counted one person: America's only town with a population of one.
To stay a town, someone has to run it. So she is mayor, clerk and treasurer, and files a road plan with the state every year.
She pays about 500 dollars in taxes, to herself, to keep three streetlights and the water on. As clerk, she signs her own tavern's liquor licence.
Beside the bar, a shed holds the 5,000-book library her husband left. A town of one: a mayor, a bar, a library. Just no voters.

description:
What if a town had a population of one? Monowi, Nebraska was a railroad town of about 150 people in the 1930s, with shops, restaurants and a jail. As farming declined, people left or died; after the last resident's husband died in 2004, the 2010 US Census recorded a population of one, the only incorporated town in the country with a single inhabitant.
To keep the village incorporated, its sole resident serves as mayor, clerk, treasurer and secretary, files an annual road plan with the state to qualify for funding, collects about 500 dollars in taxes from herself to keep the streetlights and water running, and approves her own tavern's liquor and tobacco licences. A 320-square-foot library beside the bar holds about 5,000 of her late husband's books.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The library runs on an honour system: take a book, bring it back when you are done. What should we run through next: a country with no capital city? Drop your own what-if below.
